title: Valley of Flowers
content:
Take an exquisite journey to the Valley of Flowers, a UNESCO World Heritage Site tucked in the Himalayas. This trip provides an unforgettable experience with its stunning views, bright carpets of over 600 flower species, and clean terrain. As you cross snow bridges and stone-paved trails, you'll see flowing waterfalls, peaceful rivers, and a diverse range of flora and animals, including rare species such as the blue poppy and Himalayan monal. The Valley of Flowers is ideal for nature lovers, photographers, and adventure seekers, offering a revitalizing vacation into one of nature's most gorgeous paradises.

 

Why this Trek?

 

  1. Carpet of Colors: Experience unparalleled floral diversity with over 600 species of flowers, including rare orchids, poppies, and primulas. 
  2. Nature's Beauty: Enjoy scenic trails with breathtaking views of the Himalayas and lush green forests. 
  3. UNESCO World Heritage Site: Visit a globally recognized site known for its exceptional natural beauty and biodiversity. 
  4. Photographer's Dream: Capture stunning landscapes featuring vibrant flowers, majestic mountains, and crystal-clear streams. 
  5. Spiritual Retreat: Reconnect with nature in the valley's serene environment, perfect for meditation and introspection.

[{"icon":"fa fa-check","title":"Best Time to Visit","desc":"

The best time to visit the Valley of Flowers is between July and September. During these months, the valley transforms into a vibrant landscape with over 600 species of blooming flowers. July offers a mix of melting snow and budding blooms, August brings peak floral diversity amid lush greenery, and September provides clear skies and a serene atmosphere. Daytime temperatures range from 10°C to 18°C, while nights can drop to 3°C to 5°C.

"},{"icon":"fa fa-check","title":"How to Reach Base Camp","desc":"

By Flight

The nearest airport to Rishikesh is Jolly Grant Airport in Dehradun, located about 20 kilometers away. This airport is well-connected to major cities like Delhi, Mumbai, and Bangalore through regular flights. Upon arrival at the airport, you can take a taxi, which takes approximately 45 minutes to reach Rishikesh. Alternatively, local buses might be available but are less frequent.

By Train

Rishikesh has its own railway station, Rishikesh Railway Station, which is conveniently located in the city. While this station handles limited trains, the nearby Haridwar Junction, just 25 kilometers away, offers excellent connectivity to major cities like Delhi, Kolkata, and Mumbai. From Haridwar, you can hire a taxi or take a local bus to Rishikesh, which takes around 30–45 minutes. Trains like the Yoga Express and Dehradun Express are popular choices for travelers.

By Bus

 

Rishikesh is well-connected by road, and buses are a convenient option. From Delhi, which is about 240 kilometers away, both private and state-run Volvo buses operate from Kashmiri Gate ISBT. The journey takes approximately 6–7 hours, depending on traffic conditions. Additionally, regular buses from nearby cities like Dehradun and Haridwar make reaching Rishikesh easy and affordable.

Pack smart, trek safe!

Ensure you're prepared for every adventure with this essential checklist of gear and supplies. Whether you're a beginner or a seasoned trekker, the right equipment makes all the difference. Download checklist's pdf here

 

Basic Gear

Backpack with Rain Cover (40 - 50 ltr) Comfortable Shoulder Straps
Day pack with Rain Cover 20 - 30 ltr (If off-load opted)
Walking stick Advisable (At least one)
Water Bottle / Hydration pack 2 Bottles(1 liter each), Hydration Pack 1 (Pack) + Bottle
Small size tiffin/lunch box 1 Nos
Snacks Energy bars, dry fruits, electral/ors
Personal Medical Kit Consult your doctor

 

Clothing

T-Shirt (Synthetic quick dry) 1 Full & 1 Half sleeves
Fleece T-shirt 1 Nos
Wind stopper / Fleece jacket 1 Nos
Windproof Jacket 1 Nos
Down feather / Hollow jacket 1 Nos
Thermal inner (Upper and Lower) 1 Nos
Trek Pant (Synthetic quick dry) 1 Nos
Wind stopper / Fleece Pant Not required
Waterproof gloves Not required
Fleece / woollen gloves 1 Pair
Poncho / waterproof Jacket and pant 1 Nos

 

Head Gears

Head torch 1 Nos. (Avoid Hand torch)
Sun cap 1 Nos. (One that covers the neck as well)
Woolen cap 1 Nos.
Balaclava Not required
Buff / Neck-gaiters 1 Nos
Sunglasses UV with dark side cover, People who wear spectacles - (A)- Use contact lenses | (B)- Photo chromatic glasses

 

Foot Gears

Trekking shoes 1 Pair (Waterproof, high ankle with good grip)
Floaters / flip-flops 1 Pair
Cotton socks 6 pairs
Woollen socks 1 pairs
Gaiters 1 Pair (TTH provides when required)
Micro spikes 1 Pair (TTH provides when required)

 

Personal Utilities

Sunscreen cream 1 Nos
Moisturiser 1 Nos
Chap-stick / Lip balm 1 Nos
Toothbrush and toothpaste 1 Nos
Toilet paper & Wipes 1 Nos
Soap / hand sanitizers 1 Nos
Antibacterial powder 1 Nos
Quick dry towel 1 Nos

"},{"icon":"fa fa-check","title":"Quick Facts about Valley of Flowers","desc":"

Last ATM Information

  • Joshimath is the last town where you’ll find ATMs from major private and public sector banks, some with branches.
  • Cash availability in Joshimath ATMs can be limited, so it’s better to withdraw cash from Rishikesh.
  • Recommended cash to carry: Rs 4,000-5,000 for transport, rental gear deposits, and personal expenses.
  • If planning a visit to Badrinath after the trek, carry additional cash.

faqs: [{"title":"What is the best time to visit the Valley of Flowers?","content":"The best time to visit is between July and September when the flowers are in full bloom, transforming the valley into a vibrant, colorful landscape."},{"title":"How difficult is the Valley of Flowers trek?","content":"The trek is considered moderate, with a mix of gradual and steep ascents on stone-paved paths. It is suitable for beginners with good physical fitness."},{"title":"What should I pack for the Valley of Flowers trek?","content":"Pack essentials such as sturdy trekking shoes, warm clothing (3 layers), rain gear, a first-aid kit, water bottles, snacks, and a camera. Lodges provide warm blankets."},{"title":"Is camping allowed in the Valley of Flowers?","content":"No, camping inside the Valley of Flowers is not allowed. Trekkers stay in guest houses at Ghangaria, the base camp for the trek."},{"title":"How do I reach the base camp for the Valley of Flowers trek?","content":"You can reach the base camp by flying to Dehradun or Delhi, then taking a bus or taxi to Rishikesh. From Rishikesh, you drive to Govindghat and then trek to Ghangaria."},{"title":"Are there any medical facilities available on the trek?","content":"Basic medical facilities are available at Ghangaria, but it's advisable to carry a personal first-aid kit and any necessary medications."},{"title":"What kind of wildlife can I expect to see?","content":"You may encounter a variety of flora and fauna, including the Himalayan monal, snow leopards, and numerous species of birds and butterflies."},{"title":"Is the Valley of Flowers suitable for solo travelers?","content":"Yes, the trek is suitable for solo travelers. However, it's recommended to join a guided trek for safety and companionship."},{"title":"Can I visit Hemkund Sahib during the Valley of Flowers trek?","content":"Yes, the trek to Hemkund Sahib can be included in your itinerary. It involves a steep ascent and offers spiritual and scenic experiences."},{"title":"What are the accommodation options during the trek?","content":"Accommodation is provided in shared guest houses at Ghangaria. These are basic but comfortable, with essential amenities and warm blankets."}]

itinerary: [{"desc":"Haridwar to Govindghat via Joshimath","title":"Day 01","content":"Around 7 am, gather at the pre-determined spot in Haridwar, where a representative will welcome you and provide a brief overview of your journey. You will then embark on a long, scenic uphill drive from Haridwar to Govindghat. En route, you’ll pass through Devaprayag, witnessing the sacred confluence of the Bhagirathi and Alaknanda Rivers, forming the River Ganges. The roads, carved from the mountain's edges, offer views of the river flowing through the deep gorge below. You will also pass through Joshimath, a midpoint for other religious pilgrimage sites. Arrive in Govindghat in the evening and take a halt for the night.","image_id":"treks/valley-of-flower-trek/valley-of-flower-greenery.png"},{"desc":"Govindghat to Ghangaria","title":"Day 02","content":"Start your day with a hearty meal, enjoying the stunning lush green mountain views. You will then be driven to Poolna, a nearby town, where your trek to Ghangaria begins. Follow the well-defined trail that winds through a lush green forest and alongside the beautiful Lakshman Ganga River. Take a moment to appreciate the volunteers who keep the trail clean and well-maintained. Along the way, stop at various dhabas for refreshments and to refill your water bottles. After a gentle 9 km ascent, you will arrive in Ghangaria, a small village surrounded by mountains. Check into your hotel and explore the beautiful surroundings. Enjoy a delicious dinner of local cuisines in Ghangaria before calling it a day.","image_id":"treks/valley-of-flower-trek/valley-of-flower-greenery-with-cloud.png"},{"desc":"Excursion to the Valley of Flowers","title":"Day 03","content":"Start your day with a wholesome breakfast. Today, you will ascend to a height of 3,505 meters to reach the Valley of Flowers. A single glimpse of the verdant landscape will transport you to a paradise adorned with colorful flowers. Take a moment to savor this breathtaking sight, one of nature’s finest creations that will uplift your soul. Continue further into the valley to witness thousands of vibrant flowers in full bloom. Although it will be hard to leave this heavenly view, you must begin your return trek to Ghangaria in time to arrive before dusk. Enjoy a sumptuous dinner and call it a night.","image_id":"treks/valley-of-flower-trek/valley-of-flower-scene.png"},{"desc":"Excursion to Hemkund Sahib","title":"Day 04","content":"Wake up early to the harmonious sounds of people chanting bhajans and enjoy a hot cup of chai. The trek to Hemkund Sahib is challenging, with steep ascents where a trekking stick can be very helpful. Take it slow, with frequent breaks to acclimate to the reduced oxygen levels at higher altitudes. Upon reaching Hemkund Sahib, a revered religious site where Guru Gobind Singh is believed to have meditated, soak in the serene atmosphere surrounded by seven snow-capped mountains and the pristine Hemkund lake. In the late afternoon, begin the steep descent back to Ghangaria, mindful of the unpredictable weather that can bring sudden cloud cover and rain. Upon returning, savor a dinner under the starry sky and enjoy an overnight stay at the hotel.","image_id":"treks/valley-of-flower-trek/hemkund-sahib-gurudwara.png"},{"desc":"Ghangaria To Govindghat","title":"Day 05","content":"After enjoying breakfast in the morning, begin the gentle 9 km descent back to Poolna along the same trail you trekked earlier. From Poolna, a cab will transport you the 4 km distance back to Govindghat. If you wish, you can opt for an evening tour of the picturesque Auli. Return to your hotel in Govindghat later in the evening for an overnight stay.","image_id":"treks/valley-of-flower-trek/valley-of-flower-cloud-scenery.png"},{"desc":"Govindghat to Haridwar","title":"Day 06","content":"Depart from Govindghat early for your journey back to Haridwar. The Valley of Flowers trekking package concludes here; carry with you a mosaic of unforgettable memories.","image_id":"treks/valley-of-flower-trek/valley-of-flower-trek.png"}]
